item.title: Packed test schedule in Australia is ominous for Black Caps quicks
item.description: ANALYSIS: Four tests within 31 days across Australia is bound to test the bodies of NZ’s pace bowlers - and history is not in our favour.

item.title: Cost-conscious Wellington council slashes $600k Civic Square activity budget
item.description: Plans that would have seen Wellington ratepayers fork out more than half a million for activities in the recently re-opened Civic Square have been dumped in favour of a $250,000 spend.

item.title: New Zealand ready to help secure Hormuz Strait - but how?
item.description: Labour has accused the coalition of signing New Zealand up for war, while Foreign Affairs Minister Winston Peters says that’s “absolute crap”.

item.title: Ministers differ over why Government rejected WHO rules on pandemics
item.description: Health Minister Simeon Brown and Foreign Affairs Minister Winston Peters signed a document together to reject the WHO amendments but disagree on why they signed it.

item.title: Wellington’s water shake‑up: What it means for your wallet
item.description: New water bills will surge from $200 to $566 a month within a decade, as Tiaki Wai tackles ageing pipes and decades of underinvestment.

item.title: Auckland islands’ petrol pain: Jerry cans, hard choices and $4 fuel
item.description: As petrol prices surge, Waiheke residents and businesses brace for the knock-on cost while Great Barrier faces an even starker reality; no public transport, few alternatives and fuel already well past $4 a litre.

item.title: When petrol money politics meets hard fiscal limits
item.description: ANALYSIS: Nicola Willis has moved to cushion the blow of rising fuel prices — but the policy underscores how constrained the Government really is

item.title: The rising cost of diesel adds a $7 million cost to NZ a day, trucking body says
item.description: The speed at which the cost of diesel is rising is unprecedented, the head of a large trucking company says.

item.title: Vacant and forgotten: Evicted family’s home left untouched
item.description: In late 2024, Lynn Phillips was evicted from her government-owned home due to planned renovations, which had a profound effect on her mental health. Fifteen months later, the renovations are still yet to begin.

item.title: NZ-born US firm Halter hits US$2b valuation on Peter Thiel-led funding round
item.description: Halter will use the capital on funding towards its expansion in North and South America, and the UK and Ireland.
